title: Control of barnyard grass in rice crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of barnyard grass in rice crop fields - Vietnam
Echinochloa crus-galli Cỏlồng vực nước, cỏgạo, cỏMỹ

Prevention: Only use certified seed to avoid introduction through contamination.
Clean equipment and farm machinery after working in an infested area to prevent seed spread.
Do not use potentially contaminated materials, e.g. fill dirt, hay, soil, or irrigation water.
Do not use farmyard manure from infested areas; it can carry seeds.
Thoroughly prepare land under wet or dry conditions to reduce infestations.
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events.
Prevent flowering - most recurring infestations are due to new seed rather than the soil seed bank.
Maintain water levels at 3-5cm after rice transplanting or sowing for 3-5 days as the best way to minimize seed germination and seedling growth.
Monitoring: Annual grass, spreading or stiffly erect, tufted or reclining at base; 0.3-2m high.
Leaves: dark green, linear and flat; 10−65cm long and 5-30mm wide.
Inflorescences branched, upright or nodding (10-25cm long) with flowerheads ('branches', ca. 5cm long).
Monitor the field weekly during the first 30 days after transplanting/ sowing and consider direct control if present.
Look our for the weed in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread seeds.
Direct Control: Hand-pull or hoe, removing entire root system.
Mowing is unlikely to be effective.
Use repeated shallow tillage to reduce weed emergence and removal of young plants.

Flood transplanting rice fields with 10-15cm of water (water levels to reach to 2/3 of plant height) when transplanting, maintain for at least 10-15 days after transplanting; flood sowing rice fields after sowing with 5-7cm of water for 5-10 days (depending on season), afterwards raise water levels according to plant height (up to 2/3 of plant height) for 10-15 days.
Place mulch over areas where weed is expect to grow – keeps soil cool and surpresses germination.
Cut the weed's flowers/panicle to prevent seed set.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
Various studies have reported resistance against various pesticides.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
The use of pre- and post-emergence herbicides refers to the emergence of the weed.
